info.title: Edge CLI
info.description: The `edge-cli` command line and the `edge-engine` JSON REST API, documented together. Every operation carries an `x-cli` extension naming the command that drives it.

tags.name: Engine
tags.description: Lifecycle and configuration of the `edge-engine` daemon. None of these have an `edge-core-js` equivalent — they describe the daemon itself — and none need a session.

tags.name: Context
tags.description: Calls on the shared `EdgeContext`: local device state and login-server queries that do not need a session. Each route is named after the core call it fronts.

tags.name: Login
tags.description: Every route here is named after its `context.*` call. Every successful login returns a [Session](#schema-Session) and registers it in the engine, so later calls only need the `sessionId`. The CLI writes that id to `session.json` automatically.

tags.name: Account
tags.description: Calls on a logged-in `EdgeAccount`, addressed by `sessionId`. Every route here can also return `401 INVALID_SESSION` or `401 SESSION_EXPIRED`; those are not repeated per endpoint.

tags.name: Credentials
tags.description: Password, PIN, username and recovery changes on a logged-in account. Each route is named after its `account.*` call and takes that call’s parameters.

tags.name: Two-factor authentication
tags.description: OTP state and the reset flow a user falls back on after losing their authenticator.

tags.name: Login vouchers
tags.description: When 2FA blocks a login, the login server issues a voucher an already-trusted device can approve or reject.

tags.name: Approving a QR login
tags.description: The other side of `POST /request-edge-login`: a logged-in account inspecting and approving a login somebody scanned.

tags.name: Keys
tags.description: Raw key infrastructure beneath the wallet API. Several of these return private key material, and the engine has no transport auth — treat any process that can reach the socket as fully trusted.

tags.name: Wallets
tags.description: Account-level wallet listing and creation, then per-wallet calls under `/account/{sessionId}/wallets/{walletId}/`. The `{walletId}` segment is scope — it is the receiver of the core call — and accepts a unique prefix, so these routes can also return `404 WALLET_NOT_FOUND` or `409 AMBIGUOUS_WALLET_ID`.

tags.name: Tokens
tags.description: Which tokens a wallet tracks. “Enabled” tokens are the ones the wallet syncs balances for; “detected” ones were seen on-chain but are not yet enabled.

tags.name: Transactions
tags.description: Reading transaction history, exporting it, and editing its metadata.

tags.name: Spending
tags.description:
Two ways to send funds. `POST …/spend` does the whole thing in one call. The staged workflow — `make-spend` → `sign-tx` → `broadcast-tx` → `save-tx` — hands back an [object handle](#object-handles) at each step so you can inspect fees before committing.

Every body here accepts either a full `spendInfo` object or the flatter convenience fields the CLI uses.

tags.name: Swap
tags.description: Cross-asset exchange. Quotes are live objects held server-side under a `swap_` handle, so approving one means naming its `objectId` rather than re-uploading the quote.

tags.name: Payment URIs
tags.description: Parsing and building BIP21-style payment URIs through the wallet’s own plugin, so chain-specific quirks are handled for you.

tags.name: Exchange rates
tags.description: Historical and current rates through the same `rates3` / `rates4` batching queue the GUI uses. No session required.

tags.name: Data store
tags.description: The account’s synced key-value store, where plugins keep their own state. One route per `EdgeDataStore` method. Values are opaque strings; encoding is the caller’s business.

tags.name: Admin
tags.description: **Debugging only — not for production apps.** These reach into `context.$internalStuff`, the private surface of `edge-core-js`, and can corrupt an account’s synced repos. They take no `sessionId`: they act on the context, not on a logged-in account.

post.description:
**Core call:** _none — Engine lifecycle. Internally calls context.close()._

**Command line**

```
engine-stop
```

Logs out every session, closes the context, unlinks the socket and run-file, then exits. The engine answers before it starts tearing down, so a response is not proof the process is gone.

get.description:
**Core call:** _none — Engine-side fan-out. `core.log` frames carry core’s onLog output._

**Command line**

```
subscribe [--type=<eventType>]
```

Server-Sent Events. Handled directly in `server.ts` rather than through the router, so there is no command — attach with `curl -N` or any SSE client.

flags.doc: Repeatable client-side filter; the engine always sends every event the scope allows.

x-cli.notes: Streams newline-delimited JSON and runs until interrupted. Exits 0 on SIGINT, 3 when a session ended the stream, 7 when the engine went away.

get.x-core-note: Engine-side fan-out. `core.log` frames carry core’s onLog output.

200.description: `text/event-stream`. Each frame is `event: <type>` then `data: <json>`. The stream opens with a `: ok` comment.

post.description:
**Core call:** `context.requestEdgeLogin`

**Command line**

```
request-edge-login
```

Asks the login server for a lobby another logged-in Edge device can approve. The returned `lobbyId` is what goes in the QR code.

x-cli.notes: Prints the pending login, then polls `GET /v1/login/edge/{pendingId}` every 2 s for up to 5 minutes. On `done` it stores the session and exits `0`; on `error` or `closed` it exits non-zero.

requestBody.description: None. The engine always calls `requestEdgeLogin({})`.

get.description:
**Core call:** _none — Engine state for an in-flight requestEdgeLogin; core exposes it as EdgePendingEdgeLogin properties._

**Command line**

```
request-edge-login
```

Once `state` reaches `done` the engine creates the session itself, so the response carries a ready-to-use `session`.

x-cli.summary: Polled internally by `request-edge-login`; not separately invocable.

get.x-core-note: Engine state for an in-flight requestEdgeLogin; core exposes it as EdgePendingEdgeLogin properties.

get.description:
**Core call:** _none — GUI code (src/util/localAccountSettings), reached through account.localDisklet._

**Command line**

```
local-settings
```

Device-local account settings, stored in `Settings.json` on `account.localDisklet`. They are **not synced** — a phone and a CLI have separate copies unless they share an Edge data directory. Every setting is listed below; there is one today.

x-cli.summary: With no flag, reads the current value.

parameters.name: sessionId
parameters.description: From a successful login. The CLI supplies this from `session.json`, `--session`, or `EDGE_CLI_SESSION`.

spamFilterOn.description: Hide spam transactions in `get-transactions` results. Defaults to `true`, matching the GUI. The filter hides rows; it never changes stored metadata.

post.description:
**Core call:** _none — GUI code (src/util/localAccountSettings)._

**Command line**

```
local-settings [--spam-filter-on=true|false]
```

Writes device-local account settings. Every option is listed below; `spamFilterOn` is the only one today, and new options are added here as additional fields.

x-cli.summary: With the flag, writes the value.

parameters.name: sessionId
parameters.description: From a successful login. The CLI supplies this from `session.json`, `--session`, or `EDGE_CLI_SESSION`.

requestBody.description: One field per setting. `spamFilterOn` is required; omitting it is a `400`, not a no-op, so a caller cannot accidentally clear a setting by sending an empty body.

spamFilterOn.description: Hide spam transactions in `get-transactions` results. Defaults to `true`, matching the GUI. The filter hides rows; it never changes stored metadata.

get.description:
**Core call:** `wallet.getTransactions`

**Command line**

```
get-transactions <walletId> [--token-id=<id>] [--limit=<n>] [--offset=<n>] [--start-date=<ISO>] [--end-date=<ISO>] [--search-string=<text>] [--fiat=<CODE>] [--export-format=csv,qbo,bitwave] [--out=<path>] [--bitwave-account=<id>]
```

Reads history, fills in the same display metadata and historical fiat the GUI shows, and optionally formats the result as CSV, QBO, or Bitwave. All of that happens on this one GET.

flags.doc: Use the `=` form so a timezone offset is not parsed as a new argument.
Client-side only: where to write the returned files.

x-cli.notes: `--out` is required with `--export-format` and is a usage error without it. One format writes that path; several treat it as a stem and append `.csv` / `.qbo` / `.bitwave.csv`. Paths resolve from the current directory.

parameters.name: tokenId
parameters.description: Default: `null (native)`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Omitting it returns **every** transaction from `offset` onward. Default: `unlimited`.

parameters.description: Default: `0`.

parameters.name: startDate
parameters.description: ISO-8601, or epoch milliseconds.

parameters.name: searchString
parameters.description: Matches payee, category, notes, and txid.

parameters.description: Native-amount floor. Omitted, the engine applies the GUI “Hide spam transactions” setting (`spamFilterOn`, default `true`) with a threshold near $0.001. Passing it always overrides. Filters rows only; metadata is untouched. Default: `the account’s local-settings setting`.

parameters.name: exportFormat

parameters.name: bitwaveAccountId
parameters.description: Bitwave account id. A `400` unless `exportFormat` includes `bitwave`.

200.description: The first shape without `exportFormat`, the second with it. The two are mutually exclusive — an export response carries no `transactions` array.

contents.description: The whole file as a string.

Session.description: Returned by every successful login, by session listing, and by the keepalive. `username` is absent for accounts that have no username (light accounts).

WalletSummary.description: One currency wallet. `walletId` and `id` are the same value; `id` is kept for callers written against the core object.

syncRatio.description: A **percentage string**, not a number. Absent when the wallet reports no `totalRatio`.

ObjectHandle.description: Identity for a method-bearing core value. See “Ephemeral object handles”.

TransactionHandle.description: An `ObjectHandle` carrying the transaction it refers to. Returned by every step of the staged spend workflow.

Balance.description: One asset balance. `displayAmount` is `nativeAmount` divided by the exchange denomination multiplier, to 18 decimal places.

SwapQuote.description: A swap quote, stored as a `swap_` object handle with a 5 minute TTL.

PendingEdgeLogin.description: A QR / lobby login in progress. `session` is filled once `state` reaches `done`.

lobbyId.description: The value encoded in the QR code.

OkObject.description: An acknowledgement that also names the handle the call consumed.

EnabledTokens.description: The wallet’s enabled token set after the change.

ErrorEnvelope.description: Every failure, on both transports. `error.status` always matches the HTTP status. The CLI writes this same object to stderr.
